title: Hate Speech Classifiers Learn Human-Like Social Stereotypes
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypes and biases against religious groups in the context of hate speech annotation and classification. The study measures how stereotypes of warmth and competence associated with social groups, including religious ones, affect hate speech labeling by human annotators and the error rates of a neural network classifier.
findings: Hate speech classifiers trained on human-annotated data learn human-like stereotypes. This results in biased performance, where classifiers are more likely to make prediction errors (both false-positives and false-negatives) on texts mentioning social groups that are stereotypically perceived as 'cold' and 'incompetent' in the underlying language embeddings. This pattern was observed for several minority religious groups mentioned in the study's dataset.
